update_log: Baseline initialization of India's Five-Year Plans, their underlying models, and high-frequency historical milestones for Economics Static GK.

five_year_plans.focus_area: Agriculture, price stability, power, and transport
five_year_plans.key_events: Successful plan. Five IITs were started. Major irrigation projects like Bhakra-Nangal, Hirakud, and Mettur dams were initiated.
Establishment of major steel plants at Durgapur, Bhilai, and Rourkela with foreign assistance. Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) was established.

five_year_plans.focus_area: Agriculture and making the economy self-reliant
five_year_plans.key_events: A massive failure due to the Sino-Indian War (1962), Indo-Pak War (1965), and severe drought (1965). Led to the declaration of 'Plan Holidays' (1966-1969).

five_year_plans.model: Ashok Rudra / A.S. Manne Model (Often associated with Gadgil formula)
five_year_plans.focus_area: Growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance
five_year_plans.key_events: Indira Gandhi nationalized 14 major Indian banks (1969). The Green Revolution advanced significantly. Indo-Pak War of 1971 occurred.
Terminated a year early in 1978 by the newly elected Morarji Desai (Janata Party) government, which introduced the 'Rolling Plan'.
Establishment of NABARD (1982) and EXIM Bank. Family planning was heavily promoted.

five_year_plans.model: Vakil and Brahmananda Model (Wage Goods Model)
five_year_plans.focus_area: Modernization, technology upgrading, and employment generation
five_year_plans.key_events: Introduction of the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana. Saw a rapid expansion of the private sector.

five_year_plans.focus_area: Human Resource Development (Education, Healthcare) and LPG Reforms
five_year_plans.key_events: Delayed by two years due to economic instability. Marked the beginning of Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG) under P.V. Narasimha Rao and Manmohan Singh. India joined the WTO (1995).

five_year_plans.focus_area: Growth with Social Justice and Equality
five_year_plans.key_events: Launched during India's 50th year of Independence. Pokhran-II nuclear tests occurred. Impacted by the Kargil War and the Asian Financial Crisis.

five_year_plans.focus_area: Doubling per capita income and heavily reducing poverty
five_year_plans.key_events: Highly successful in achieving its growth targets. Focused on universalizing primary education.
Focused on agriculture, education, and skill development. Right to Education (RTE) Act was enacted (2009).

five_year_plans.focus_area: Faster, sustainable, and more inclusive growth
five_year_plans.key_events: The final Five-Year Plan. In 2015, the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog.
